label: JZ Mock C · Paper 2 · Question 2
knowledgePattern: Check inequality preservation over all signs
solution:
The cube function is increasing on the real numbers. Algebraically x3−y3=(x−y)(x2+xy+y2), with the first factor nonnegative and the second nonnegative, so statement 1 is always true.

Statement 2 fails for x=1,y=−2. Statement 3 fails for x=1,y=0,z=−1, because multiplication by a negative number reverses order.

For statement 4, z2≥0, so multiplying x≥y by it preserves the inequality, including equality when z = 0. Exactly 1 and 4 hold. Answer F.

hints.title: Prove the cube comparison
hints.body: Factor x3−y3. Use the given order of x and y to check the sign of each factor.
hints.recap: To prove one quantity is at least another, show their difference is nonnegative.
hints.pitfall: Checking a few pairs cannot prove a claim for every real pair.
hints.pause: Justify the sign of the quadratic factor as well.

recall.reminder: A universal claim needs a proof; one valid counterexample is enough to disprove it.

hints.title: Check the multiplier
hints.body: In statements 3 and 4, look at what multiplies both sides. Can it be positive, zero or negative?
hints.recap: Multiplying by a negative number reverses an inequality; multiplying by zero gives equal sides.
hints.pitfall: A squared multiplier and an unsquared multiplier need separate checks.
hints.pause: Check positive, zero and negative multipliers in statements 3 and 4.
